clue.text: School of psychology finds him abusive or stroppy

indicators.note: stroppy means bad-tempered and unruly, so the words before it are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A psychology school's adherents are accused of being rude and aggressive towards a man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stroppy' (British slang for awkward, bad-tempered) signals an anagram of HIM ABUSIVE OR.
explanation.definitionFit: Behaviourism is the school of psychology that studies observable conduct rather than inner states.

clue.text: One crooning about bird — maybe more than one over here?

definitions.text: maybe more than one over here?

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the crooner's name is placed around the bird

parts.note: Bing Crosby was the most famous crooner
an owl is a bird

explanation.surface: A singer croons about a bird, perhaps several of them in this place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts OWL inside BING. In cricket an over is a set of six balls, so a spell of bowling may run to more than one over.
explanation.definitionFit: Cricket overs are delivered during a spell of bowling, the activity where they happen.

clue.text: Busy place in Delhi? Very

indicators.note: in tells us the letters sit inside the words that follow, spanning the gap

explanation.surface: A traveller asks whether Delhi is a bustling city and gets the reply 'Very'.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'DelHI VEry'.
explanation.definitionFit: A hive of activity is a bustling place, from the beehive full of working insects.

clue.text: Dean's title given to friend corruptly

parts.note: Ven., short for Venerable, is the courtesy title of senior clergy such as archdeacons
an ally is a friend

explanation.surface: A cathedral dean's honorific is bestowed on a pal through bribery.
explanation.walkthrough: VEN is the abbreviation for Venerable, used before the names of some Anglican clergy.
explanation.definitionFit: Venal means open to bribery, so acting venally is behaving in a bribable, dishonest way.

clue.text: Group playing tote, etc

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters are performed in a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A gambling crowd plays the tote and other betting games.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' signals an anagram of TOTE ETC.
explanation.definitionFit: An octette is a set of eight musicians, a musical ensemble.

clue.text: Drains will contain it

indicators.note: will contain says the letters are held within the word before it

explanation.surface: Gutters and drains are where downpour water ends up.
explanation.walkthrough: The word sits inside 'dRAINs', and the whole clue is also a plain truth: storm drains carry rainwater.
explanation.definitionFit: Water from showers runs off into drains, which carry it away.

clue.text: Nips or pins to make something last?

parts.note: read the answer phrase as instructions: the first word with its letters thrown about by the second gives either of these words

explanation.surface: Asks whether small bites or pins could prolong something.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: treat OUT as an anagram signal applied to SPIN, and you get NIPS or PINS.
explanation.definitionFit: To spin out a story or supply is to prolong it, stretching it further.

clue.text: Staff, mature people, caught in fog — inept organisation

indicators.note: caught in means the run of pieces is trapped inside the word for fog

parts.note: mist is a thin fog
to man a post is to staff it
to age is to mature
men are people

explanation.surface: Workers, older folk and others lost in a fog: a bungled set-up.
explanation.walkthrough: MAN, AGE and MEN go inside MIST.
explanation.definitionFit: Poor handling of a business is bad administration, a failure to run things competently.

clue.text: Confused mass possibly alarming to ego

indicators.note: possibly hints the letters that follow could form something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: A jumbled heap that might alarm one's sense of self.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' signals an anagram of ALARMING TO EGO.
explanation.definitionFit: An agglomeration is a jumbled heap gathered without order.

clue.text: I've won battles about name for describing design in cloth?

indicators.note: about here means the scrambled letters surround the single letter
battles means the letters before it fight and scramble into a new order

explanation.surface: A fighter claims victory in battles and talks of a name for a textile pattern.
explanation.walkthrough: 'battles' gives an anagram of IVEWON (I've won), IWOVEN, and 'about' places N inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A pattern that is inwoven is worked into the fabric as it is woven, not printed on afterwards.

clue.text: Slight noise: introduce lubricant (it's working)

indicators.note: introduce means put the lubricant into the noise word

parts.note: a ting is a light ringing sound
oil is a lubricant

explanation.surface: A machine squeaks faintly; add some oil and it runs.
explanation.walkthrough: OIL goes inside TING.
explanation.definitionFit: Toiling is labouring hard, so a synonym of busy at work.

clue.text: Main road runs between motorways — result is to produce injuries

indicators.note: runs between says the road is laid down between the two motorways

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for a motorway, as in the M1, and the plural gives two
the A1, read as AI, is Britain's longest main road, the Great North Road

explanation.surface: A trunk road is squeezed between motorways, and the result is road casualties.
explanation.walkthrough: The A1 is written AI and placed between two Ms, giving MAIM. The answer listing prints MAIN, a misprint: no parse gives MAIN, and 'to produce injuries' defines MAIM.
explanation.definitionFit: To maim is to wound someone seriously, inflicting lasting harm.

clue.text: Fine old instrument, one in the wind section

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils
the lute is an old stringed instrument

explanation.surface: A fine antique instrument sits among the orchestra's wind players.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wind section' looks like weather but means the woodwind of an orchestra.
explanation.definitionFit: The flute is a woodwind instrument, so it belongs among the orchestra's wind players.

clue.text: Get to a hundred, but no more?

definitions.text: Get to a hundred, but no more?

parts.words: Get to a hundred, but no more?
parts.note: sounds like a cricketer making a century, but means water reaching 100 degrees Celsius, the point beyond which it gets no hotter

explanation.surface: A batsman reaches a century and then is out.
explanation.walkthrough: Water heated to 100°C stops rising in temperature while it changes to steam.
explanation.definitionFit: Water reaches 100 degrees Celsius when it starts bubbling into steam.

clue.text: I agree to eliminate Latin country

indicators.note: to eliminate tells us one letter is taken out of the word for agree

parts.note: accounts that tally agree

explanation.surface: Someone agrees to drop Latin from the curriculum of a nation.
explanation.walkthrough: TALLY loses its L, leaving TALY after I.
explanation.definitionFit: Italy is a European nation.

clue.text: Annoying youngster holds piece of clover leaf

indicators.note: holds means the youngster word grips the next piece inside it

parts.note: a brat is an annoying child

indicators.note: piece of here takes just the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A naughty child clutches a bit of clover.
explanation.walkthrough: C, the first letter of clover, goes inside BRAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A bract is a modified leaf growing at the base of a flower.

clue.text: Have thing about start and finish of lullaby every evening?

indicators.note: about here means the letters of the word that precedes it are turned around into a new order
start and finish of takes the opening and closing letters of the following word

explanation.surface: Someone obsessed with lullabies sings them each night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges THING to NIGHT; L and Y are the first and last letters of 'lullaby'. 'Have a thing about' reads as an obsession.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done nightly happens each night, after dark.

clue.text: Correction of traitor beset by hesitations

indicators.note: beset by means the traitor is surrounded by the hesitation sounds

parts.note: er is a hesitation noise
um is another hesitation noise
a rat is a traitor or informer

explanation.surface: A newspaper correction about a turncoat is delivered with much stammering.
explanation.walkthrough: RAT goes between ER and UM, two sounds of hesitation.
explanation.definitionFit: An erratum is an error listed for amendment in a printed work.

clue.text: Weather-beaten Derek phoned back

indicators.note: back says the whole run of pieces is read from right to left

parts.note: Del is the short form of Derek, as in Del Boy
rang means phoned

explanation.surface: A rugged-looking Derek returned a call.
explanation.walkthrough: DEL + RANG, read backwards as one run, gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Gnarled means rough and twisted, like old wood or skin worn by the elements.

clue.text: Road ran off into small principality

indicators.note: off suggests the letters go awry and are rearranged

explanation.surface: A road veers off into a tiny mountain state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' signals an anagram of ROAD RAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Andorra is a tiny principality in the Pyrenees.

clue.text: I'd help to change conservative description of oracle

indicators.note: to change tells us the letters before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone offers to help a Tory change how they describe a prophet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to change' rearranges IDHELP to DELPHI, then C follows.
explanation.definitionFit: The oracle at Delphi was the most famous in Greece, so delphic describes oracular, ambiguous pronouncements.

clue.text: Shield appearing to deform on right

parts.note: to buckle is to bend out of shape

explanation.surface: A shield seems to warp on its right side.
explanation.walkthrough: BUCKLE then R.
explanation.definitionFit: A buckler is a small round shield held by a handle.

clue.text: The French company lie about type of lens

indicators.note: about here means the whole run of pieces is turned round and read backwards

parts.note: la is French for the
a fib is a lie

explanation.surface: A French firm tells untruths about a kind of spectacle lens.
explanation.walkthrough: LA + CO + FIB, reversed as one run, gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Bifocal spectacle lenses have two parts, for near and distant sight.

clue.text: Plant from experimental establishment I consumed

parts.note: a lab is a laboratory where experiments are done
ate means consumed

explanation.surface: A specimen from a research laboratory that the speaker ate.
explanation.walkthrough: LAB + I + ATE.
explanation.definitionFit: A labiate is a member of the mint family, with lipped flowers.

clue.text: One foolish over longish skirt

indicators.note: over means the pieces are turned over and read backwards

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
dim means foolish

explanation.surface: A silly person in a calf-length skirt.
explanation.walkthrough: I + DIM read backwards gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A midi is a skirt reaching mid-calf, longer than a mini.

clue.text: Features seen in capital of Tibet, in elevated location

indicators.note: features seen in says the letters appear within the words that follow, across their joins

explanation.surface: Sights in Lhasa, high on the Tibetan plateau.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'capitAL OF Tibet'. 'capital of' tempts you to take T, but the whole phrase holds the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Aloft means high up, in the air above.

clue.text: Help from a telephone company installing electronics, initially

indicators.note: installing means the phone firm puts the next piece inside itself

parts.note: BT, British Telecom, is the UK telephone company

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: Getting assistance from a phone company fitting electronics.
explanation.walkthrough: E, the first letter of 'electronics', goes inside BT, after A.
explanation.definitionFit: To abet is to assist, usually in wrongdoing.

clue.text: Outer part of some quarter in dispute

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: The outer section of a district that is under contention.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'quarteR IN Dispute'.
explanation.definitionFit: A rind is the tough outer skin of fruit or cheese.

clue.text: Creature seen in forest again

indicators.note: seen in tells us the letters appear within the words that follow

explanation.surface: An animal is spotted in the woods once more.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'foreST AGain'.
explanation.definitionFit: A stag is a male deer, an animal of the woods.

clue.text: No women in opulent city

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in means the women piece goes inside the word for opulent

parts.note: rich means opulent

explanation.surface: A wealthy city without any women.
explanation.walkthrough: W goes inside RICH, after NO.
explanation.definitionFit: Norwich is a cathedral city in Norfolk, eastern England.

clue.text: Cross animal, feline, upset a lot

parts.note: a cat is a feline

indicators.note: upset means the following letters are knocked over into a new order

explanation.surface: An irritable crossbred animal: a cat very upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges A LOT to TALO, after CAT. 'Cross' looks like angry, but means hybrid.
explanation.definitionFit: A cattalo is a hybrid of domestic cattle and American bison.

clue.text: Sent, as they say, for Wasser?

definitions.text: Sent, as they say, for Wasser?

parts.words: Sent, as they say, for Wasser?
parts.note: 'sent' spoken sounds like scent, a perfume, and Wasser is German for water, pointing to a perfumed water named after a German city

explanation.surface: Someone was dispatched to fetch water, in German.
explanation.walkthrough: The fragrance's French name means 'water of Cologne', the German city where it was first made.
explanation.definitionFit: This toilet water is a light perfume, literally the water from Cologne.
